To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the physical activity recommendations for older adults to improve or maintain cognitive health are to engage in 150 minutes per week of moderate intensity physical activity, such as brisk walking, or 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity physical activity, such a jogging.

(a) physical activity is beneficial for the brain in healthy older adults and in those with mild cognitive impairment; (b) physical activity is safe for older adults, even for those who are frail; (c) physical activity is not harmful to the brain in older adults with dementia, but it is not known if physical activity is helpful in these populations; (d) exercise is beneficial for the brains of children and young adults, and physical activity is also beneficial for the brain of older adults;
physical activity has beneficial effects on cognition in older persons and is safe.

the development of novel, non-invasive, and non-pharmacological approaches that will help improve cognitive and brain health in older adults.
the role of physical activity and physical fitness on cognitive function and the brain.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current evidence supports a recommendation that older adults engage in regular aerobic physical activity, as well as resistance exercise, and that these activities can help maintain and improve brain health and reduce risk for cognitive decline.

physical activity is associated with a reduced risk of cognitive decline and dementia, with the greatest benefits seen in the prevention and treatment of mild cognitive impairment, and that the benefits are greater in those at higher risk of cognitive impairment.

regular physical activity is beneficial for cognitive function in healthy older adults and that the most effective type and intensity of physical activity for cognitive function in older adults has not yet been identified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physical activity has a beneficial effect on the brain.
regular physical activity, including resistance training, can improve cognition and reduce risk of cognitive decline.
regular physical activity is safe for older adults and can help maintain or improve cognitive function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physical activity can be beneficial to the brain, and it should be encouraged in older adults.
the current physical activity guidelines for older adults can be safely followed by most older adults.
older adults can benefit from physical activity, even if they are sedentary or have chronic medical conditions.
